Lauren Crowl is a redshirt senior from Eagan, Minn. A three-time Academic All-B1G honoree, Lauren has played in 80 matches at the 'U', tallying 115 kills, 65 blocks and 71 digs.

She's helped the Gophers four NCAA Tournaments, including an Elite Eight and a Sweet 16.

A two-time Big Ten Distinguished Scholar, Crowl graduated last December with a degree in strategic communications and business management. She will graduate this December with her master's in sports management.

Crowl is undecided on her plans after finishing her volleyball career at Minnesota.

Thank you for being a Golden Gopher, Lauren!

caption: Happy 22nd Birthday to my beautiful wife, the woman who changed my whole world the moment she walked into it. I love celebrating you because there’s so much to celebrate. Your heart, your strength, your laugh, your loyalty, your faith, your beauty inside and out… everything about you blows me away every single day. You are my comfort and my excitement all at once, the peace I always needed and the love I always prayed for. Thank you for being the rock in our home, my biggest supporter, my favorite teammate, and the person who sees the best in me even on the days I can’t see it myself. Thank you for choosing me, through the challenges, the distance, the chaos, and the growth. 22 is YOUR year, and I hope it’s filled with answered prayers, doors opening, and confidence in who you are becoming. I’m going to be beside you the whole way, cheering for you, protecting you, and loving you harder than the day before. You deserve every good thing this life can offer, and I’ll give you the world. You are my soulmate, my best friend, my forever girl. I can’t wait for every birthday we get to celebrate for the rest of our lives. So here’s to the most gorgeous, strong, loving woman I know… My wife. My world. My everything. Happy Birthday baby, I love you forever 🤍♾️

caption:
Proverbs 3:5-6: “Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to Him, and He will make your paths straight.”

Put God First.

I can’t even begin to describe the impact the Lord has made on my life this past week at UTC. God has never once given up on me — even when I’ve felt unworthy and undeserving. His grace met me exactly where I was and in ways I never expected.

This past week, I was pushed beyond my physical and mental limits. Yet through it all, I found myself gripping more tightly to my spiritual strength. Philippians 4:13 — “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me” — became more than a verse; it became real, active, and alive in me.

God pointed me in so many directions this weekend that truly changed my life. He broke down walls I didn’t even know I had built, revealing a deeper purpose and calling.

I’ve come to fully surrender to the Lord, realizing that my identity and worth are not found in my sport, my accomplishments, or my performance. My identity is rooted in Christ alone. That truth has set me free.

I am beyond thankful for my team and everyone else surrounding me that supported me and stood by my side through it all. 

Jesus is enough. He always has been — and always will be. God is so good! 

I AM FULLY SATISFIED IN CHRIST!

caption:
What joy it is to stand in the presence of the One True King, surrounded by my brothers and sisters in Christ. This has truly been the best week of the year. God knew exactly how much I needed UTC. Experiencing this week from an intern perspective was a soul-refreshing reminder of His love — to witness Jesus running to embrace His sheep, arms wide open, smile radiant with grace. Just a small glimpse of what eternity looks like.

Thank you, Jesus, for gently reminding me that without You, I am nothing. Help me remember to lay down my pride daily and surrender fully to Your guidance and grace.

The F.E.L.L.O.W.S.H.I.P. this week has been so genuine and life-giving. Until next time @theultimatetrainingcamp !! 

Thanks @visualxcarlo for capturing this week!

caption:
What a privilege it is to be a part of this intern group. Having the opportunity to be surrounded by an environment of people seeking and growing the kingdom of God is so special and something I couldn’t pass up. 

Thank you Lord for reminding me I don’t need to do anything but humbly walk with you while putting you and others before myself. To lead is to be selfless. I have so much joy when I say I have given myself to the Lord this past week to be used however He wants to, and rely on His spirit to lead me.

In these moments of pouring into others, hearing their stories, and sharing the good news with all who wants to hear it, I feel so grateful to simply be used as His vessel. I’ve learned I am powerless when it comes to changing hearts + minds and opening eyes- this can only be done in His timing and in His power.

He is always good. He is always so faithful. He’s the only healer, a fixer of brokenness. I am a testimony of His love. My full joy and satisfaction can only come from Him alone. 

Thank you UTC MN 25’ for another blessing, for all of the love, the guidance, support and amazing people. 

@visualxcarlo -check Carlo’s work out, he’s AMAZING !!

With her mobility and range of motion restored, Natalie is back on the mound at full strength, having just wrapped up her first collegiate season.

Through every moment of this last week at @theultimatetrainingcamp God was working. I hit many points of exhaustion where I had nothing left to give, but it was in that place of total weakness that I finally saw the strength of Jesus more clearly than ever before. He met me right where I was and through this I learned to fully surrender everything to Him. Surrender to His plans. Surrender my pride. Surrender my desires. Surrender to the narrow path that leads to life.

I am filled with gratitude for the call that the Lord had on my heart to attend UTC this year. I am blessed to have met some of the most amazing people who helped me grow and created relationships that will last for a lifetime. Thank you @visualxcarlo for capturing the beauty and rawness of this week for us. THANK YOU GOD for turning from the 99 to save me. For the sacrifice you made and the talent you have given me to continue to shine light on your name.
I FULLY SURRENDER. ❤️❤️❤️

caption:
Nationals 2025 🩷

Wow what an amazing and unforgettable way to wrap up my senior season!! I’m ending my JO career as a National Vault (10.0), Beam (9.75) and AA (39.275) champion!! I also earned my first perfect 10 on Vault which has been one of my goals for so long 🤗 Region 4 took home the gold as well!! This has been the best and most special 13 years ever, and I’m so thankful for all the friendships and memories gymnastics has brought me. Thank you to my teammates, coaches and family for always supporting me I love you guys sm!

Although I’m sad it’s my last JO meet, I can’t wait for what’s to come!

🔜 NCAA ❤️💛

athlete.bio: A tenacious force on the field, this Minnesota standout blends agility and strategic finesse. With a relentless drive and a spirited personality, she inspires teammates while captivating fans with her skillful play.

caption:
Over the past few weeks, I’ve been reflecting on the book of Exodus and the faithfulness of the Lord. It says “I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with ability, and intelligence, with knowledge and all craftsmanship.” (31:3) We are all created in the image of God, and He has been gracious enough to share His gifts with us not to receive honor ourselves in this world, but to radiate the glory back to the one and only who is worthy of it. 

It has been nothing short of a blessing from God to see my team embrace what it means to compete for an audience of one, and use the gifts God has given us to serve Him. Together, through trials and triumphs in gymnastics, we know our earthly riches mean nothing in comparison to our eternal treasure gifted to us through Jesus. caption:
Give Athletes More Grace. 

I have been debating sharing this for a while now, but I am a person of words, and I believe it needs to be said. 

Sports are an amazing thing in life; however, they are not our entire life. They are supposed to bring joy, but they also bring a load of physical and mental pain. Oftentimes, we push ourselves past limits—physically, mentally, emotionally—often at the cost of our own well-being. And we keep going because that is what is expected of us, even if no one sees the toll it takes. Plus, we would do anything for our team.

We are constantly judged off our performances, but people often forget that we are human—complex, emotional, fragile—and that we carry more than just the title of “athlete.” Not every day we are going to perform our best. And although we may not think it or want it to be that way, it is reality. 

Not only are we Division 1 athletes, but we are students, teammates, daughters, sisters, friends… We devote our days trying to become the best we can be in all facets of life. We not only are in the gym for 4+ hours every day, but we also have school, jobs, family, relationships, and personal time to tend to. Sometimes everything may feel like sunshine and rainbows. And other times we fall short. And that’s really ok. 

Athletes, it may be hard to see the big picture when you are so caught up in the clutter, but at the end of the day we are so much more than our sport. 🤍

caption:
“Even before he made the world, God loved us and chose us in Christ to be holy and without fault in his eyes.”
‭‭Ephesians‬ ‭1‬:‭4‬ ‭ 

I can’t even begin to put into words how much joy the spirit of the Lord showed me this past week. Surrounded by a society that places so much emphasis on finding an identity in sport, it is easy to become fixated on working towards accolades and approval from others. BUT, in reality, we only have one true identity and that is in Christ alone. 

The Lord again pointed out to me that leaning on my own strength leads to failure. During some of the most challenging moments physically, mentally, and spiritually, I fully surrendered to Him and experienced the miraculous strength and endurance that only the Lord can provide. 

I am satisfied in Christ alone for his mercy and love is endless! 

It was a blessing to be united with so many brothers and sisters in Christ that are on fire for Jesus! Seeing so many fruitful hearts and creating friendships that will last forever is truly a prayer answered. 

May we truly embrace the big dub (of worship) over the small wins throughout our sports careers!

Until next time UTC!!

Philippians 4:13 “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.”

Even though it’s such a well known verse, it felt so real to me this week at @theultimatetrainingcamp This was the best week and was truly a life changing experience in the greatest way possible. This camp pushed me so far beyond my mental, physical, and spiritual limits, I was once again reminded of how powerful it is to rely on Jesus and fully surrender to him. I am forever thankful for the community surrounding me throughout the week and for those who brought me so much joy. I found my identity in Christ and no longer my athletic performance. I am fully satisfied in Christ. 

Team 10. I truly could not have gotten through this without you guys. Having you there by my side every step of the way is something I will forever be grateful for. You all inspire me and I love you so much 💚

God is so so good!!!

caption:
“The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in him, and he helps me. My heart leaps for joy, and with my song I praise him.” 

Psalm 28:7

While there aren’t enough words to describe the experience I had at UTC, I express eternal gratitude towards these people, this place and the incomparable joy flooding my heart while being surrounded by God’s children whose hearts are on fire for the Lord. 

In competing for the approval of only one person- Jesus Christ, I felt true freedom for the first time in my life and in sport. I have exceeded the mental and physical boundaries I never thought I could reach this week. I now know this was only ever possible through the power of the Holy Spirit. Without Him I am nothing, but with Him I have strength. 

Thank you Team 9, you have shown me unconditional, authentic love all week and for that I will always be grateful. 

Amanda, I can’t thank you enough for your leadership, seed-planting, and most importantly, your persistence in convincing me to sign up for UTC. You have made a greater impact on my faith journey than you even know. 

Lord, I praise you and your name for this irreplaceable opportunity. Thank you for allowing me to be apart of an environment that helped me to flourish in living the way you intended for me to live. I need you every single day of my life, and you have never left my side. I surrender it all to you.

God is so so good.🤍

caption:
My faith journey has been a little bit of a rollercoaster ride to say the least. While I have been constantly surrounded by a faith community, I would say that my true faith journey started years later at the end of highschool. I had many experiences where I have felt the hand of God and also pulled away through times of struggle. But after going through a battle of tug of war, God finally won my heart over this past year. My eyes were opened to the heart and love that Jesus has for me. The first semester of my freshman year, I was definitely riding a sort of spiritual high. God had led me to a faith community which I had prayed about before coming to school. I was so excited about my new church family and those in which I could share my life experiences with. Everything seemed to be going just right. Second semester came, and my world was turned upside down. It started off mildly as I began to be more tentative in the gym and became fixated on the results of my performance. As the season ramped up, and we began competing every weekend, that constant crave for perfection was taking over my mind both in the gym and in the classroom. I was placing my full identity in my performance, but even perfection alone didn’t fill my empty soul and I was left constantly feeling unsatisfied, anxious, and alone. I began to not be able to sleep because my brain refused to be hushed when I lay down at night. On top of being restless, and having constant butterflies in my stomach the moment I woke up, I began to have panic attacks. I would call my mom on the phone not being able to breathe because I was so worked up and could not seem to find any inner peace. I hated school and I hated gymnastics and I was close to going home. I was placing my whole value as a human being in earthly things. I had never felt so alone. I pulled away from practically everyone and chose to leave the suffering to myself. My mom constantly had my back, and God chose to use her to bring my focus back to him.

caption:
Rafiki zangu. 🇰🇪
Oh what a blessing it is that God lets human beings cross paths! My time in Kenya so far has been nothing but a dream come true. While the scenery is jaw dropping and the wildlife is incredible, I am greatly overwhelmed by the community that the Kenyan culture is founded on. Everywhere we go we are welcomed with open arms and smiles from amazing people. Even with a partial language barrier, our love for sports is a universal language that unites us together. I have learned so much from this group of people that I strive to be like.

Anita (10) taught me the importance of focusing completely on the only one who can grant us true joy. When asked what made her happy today, she replied, “Today I am happy because God gave me the opportunity to see today. It is because of his glory that we can experience life together”. 

Maryann demonstrated true selflessness when offering to just carry my items from the field to the car. A small gesture but one that opened my eyes to a whole other concept of serving others.

My friends, you have left a mark on my life forever!
